title: PageHeader
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar and androidx.compose.material3.LargeTopAppBar with TopAppBarDefaults.exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior, MonarchIconButton actions and MonarchMenu for the overflow
summary: The top app bar is the page header: the title, the back button and the actions that apply to the whole screen, with the rest in an overflow menu. Status, details and section tabs sit below it as the first content. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: At the top of every screen. Use LargeTopAppBar for the top screen of a section, collapsing into the small bar as the person scrolls, and TopAppBar for detail screens.
whenNotToUse: Do not put status badges, key facts or a banner in the bar itself; put them in the content under it. For a record's header with navigation between records, see the record-header recipe.
api: @Composable fun TopAppBar(title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}, expandedHeight: Dp = TopAppBarDefaults.TopAppBarExpandedHeight, windowInsets: WindowInsets = TopAppBarDefaults.windowInsets, colors: TopAppBarColors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(), scrollBehavior: TopAppBarScrollBehavior? = null)

@Composable fun LargeTopAppBar(title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}, …, scrollBehavior: TopAppBarScrollBehavior? = null)
@Composable fun TopAppBarDefaults.exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior(state: TopAppBarState = rememberTopAppBarState(), canScroll: () -> Boolean = { true }, …): TopAppBarScrollBehavior
@Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(0.dp, 4.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: expanded
states.description: LargeTopAppBar shows the title large under the actions.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: As the content scrolls, the bar collapses to the small title, connected through the scroll behavior's nestedScroll.

states.name: overflow open
states.description: The More button opens a MonarchMenu with the secondary actions.

appearance: The bar uses the canvas colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the surface behind the title, the default text color for the title and icons, and the scrolled container color when content passes under it. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PageHeader draws the title, eyebrow, breadcrumbs, back link, status, details, tabs, a banner and an action row that overflows into a More menu below 640 pixels. On Android the top app bar owns the title, the back button and two or three actions, and the rest go in an overflow MonarchMenu chosen by the app. Breadcrumbs and the eyebrow are not used on phones: the back button and the navigation hierarchy replace them (use MonarchBreadcrumb only for deep hierarchies). Status, details, a banner and tabs are the first rows of the content. The web's sticky option is the default: the bar stays and collapses. iOS uses the navigation bar the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: the title is a heading for TalkBack, and the bar's icon buttons have 48dp touch targets.
Every icon-only action needs a contentDescription, such as "Add contact" and "More actions".
The back button is named "Back" and its arrow mirrors in right-to-left layouts (an autoMirror vector).
The status under the bar is said in text ("Active"), not by its color alone.
edgeCases: A long title is cut with an ellipsis in the small bar; LargeTopAppBar wraps it to two lines when expanded.
Keep at most three action icons; the rest belong in the overflow menu.
Connect the scroll behavior with Modifier.nestedScroll(scrollBehavior.nestedScrollConnection) on the Scaffold, or the bar does not collapse.
